newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: Pakistan growth seen at 5.0 pct vs 6.0 pct target.
newsitem.headline: Pakistan growth seen at 5.0 pct vs 6.0 pct target.

text.p: Pakistan's economy is likely to grow only five percent in fiscal 1996/97 (July-June) instead of six percent as targeted, its finance chief said on Thursday.
Shahid Javed Burki, finance and economic affairs adviser to caretaker Prime Minister Meraj Khalid, said tighter fiscal and monetary policies would restrain economic expansion.

"There will be some slowing down of growth," he told Reuters in an interview. "My expectation is that we will end the year with a growth rate of about five percent, rather than six percent which is what was expected."

He said he was less sure if industry would suffer as a result of the stabilisation measures of the past few months. "Probably not, because the price increases that we have induced do not form a large share of industrial input," he said.
